note: Unfortified oats, dry. USDA covers regular and quick oats in one record (shared with quick oats). Porridge made with milk or water belongs in recipes or components.
Same USDA record as rolled oats (regular and quick, not fortified). Flavoured or fortified instant oat sachets need labels.
Unprocessed (crude) wheat bran, not bran flakes cereal.
No USDA muesli record; mixes of oats, nuts, seeds and fruit vary. Use the pack label.
No USDA muesli record; fruit, nut and sugar content vary. Use the pack label.
USDA's only generic granola is a homemade recipe (oats, nuts, oil, sweetener). Commercial granola varies widely in sugar, oil and nuts, so prefer the pack label.
USDA only has branded US cornflakes; fortification is brand-specific. Use the pack label.
USDA only has branded US bran flakes; fortification and sugar are brand-specific. Use the pack label.
Wheat biscuit cereals are fortified brand formulations; USDA only has US branded shredded wheat, a different product. Use the pack label.
Generic USDA puffed rice, unsweetened but US-fortified, so macros fit plain puffed rice while iron and B vitamins may not. Sweetened crisped rice cereals need a label.
Generic USDA puffed wheat, unsweetened but US-fortified, so micronutrients may differ. Honey or sugar-coated puffed wheat needs a label.
USDA only has branded US chocolate cereals plus one generic chocolate frosted puffed corn; base grain, sugar and fortification vary. Use the pack label.
USDA only has branded US honey cereals. Use the pack label.

Assumed to be the dry short-grain white rice used for rice porridge or pudding (unenriched short-grain record). Ground rice or branded cream of rice need labels; porridge cooked with milk is a recipe.
